title: What If You Shouted on Mars? High Notes Arrive First
subject: Mars sound

scenes.text: What if you shouted on Mars? The strangest part is that high notes arrive first.
Sound there travels at about 240 meters per second. On Earth, it's about 343.
Mars's air is thin and mostly carbon dioxide, so it carries sound badly.
Perseverance's microphone found higher pitches move faster, about 250 meters per second.
So a distant orchestra would arrive out of order, high notes first, low notes late.
And it gets quiet fast: someone talking beside you would sound like they were 60 meters away.
